newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling suffers further loss under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling suffers further loss under pressure.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling suffered further losses versus the dollar on Monday and was under pressure to weaken further amid heavy dollar demand from nervous investors after the IMF cancelled a huge aid package last week, dealers said.
The shilling opened at 61.50/63.50 and then moved to a range of 62/63.25 from Friday's closing rates of 60.50/61.50 against the dollar, according to prices posted by commercial banks.

The International Monetary Fund decision to suspend a $205 million three-year loan under its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF), in a row over corruption, severely shook Kenya's foreign exchange and equity markets on Friday.
The shilling fell as low as 64.50 on Friday after opening at 59.50 but corrected to close at about 61.50 to the dollar.
Dealers said the shilling's future was bleak, adding that they were keeping wide spreads because the market was so nervous and they did not know how much volume they were going to trade.
"Pressure is there. Orders are large," a dealer from a leading bank said, adding that orders ranged from $10 million to $20 million, from both offshore investors and commercial companies.
